source_quality.text_layer: usable prose; formula glyphs and watermark marks corrupt the text layer, so every numbered equation was read from the page rasters

task_reconstruction: Hold the Great Lakes at monthly levels that balance five groups of users, then keep them there with the two dams under rain and ice, using a search, a lake-chain flow model and a controller that switches mode.

section_map.summary: summary: the five tasks, the two dams and the verdict
introduction: the uses, the two controls, the five tasks
two assumptions, each with its reason, then the notation table
the search that copies heredity and the five benefit functions
the pairwise weights and the monthly best levels
the lakes drawn as one chain
the channel formula, the doubled width and the lagged reach
rain, drying off and the calibration against recorded flows
the classical controllers and why a fixed rule fails
the forecast module and the tuning score
the 2017 comparison and the start of the rain test
the lowest lake, the side river and the city

contributions.summary: five stakeholder benefit functions weighted by pairwise ranking into one monthly target
a one-way lake chain with the flow taken from a channel formula and one lagged reach
a controller that switches mode at each dam, with two gains retuned against a 200 hour forecast

dependency_graph.carries: the monthly level the dams are told to hold
the forecast the gains are tuned against

assumptions.summary: the flow between the two joined lakes is dropped, the supplement showing them at one level
the search starts at the historical mean, hand-made shifts being far smaller than the depths
the smallest lake is treated as a river because its area is far below the others

data_and_preprocessing.summary: table 3: lake areas, mean depths and elevations, read from the raster because the text layer scrambles the rows
table 4: the five rivers, mean flow, width and depth
seasonal drying off cited to named authors, peaking near four tenths of a foot a day in autumn

models.summary: the five benefit functions and the fitness the search minimises
the lake chain: level change, the channel formula and the lagged reach
the two mode-switchable controllers and the 200 hour tuning score

verification.summary: the 2017 levels are read against the best-level band by eye
with the dams the middle lakes end about a quarter metre lower at 200 hours
a shift of about 2000 cubic metres a second moves a level by about a fifth of a metre in ten days

results_trace.summary: every lake but one has its best level below the historical mean
the lowest lake follows the downstream dam, the four above follow the upstream works
the rules hold up against the ice, but the dams can only do so much against fast change

writing_logic.summary: the summary gives each task one or two sentences and closes with two virtues
three faults of a fixed rule are listed and the design is said to answer them
the memo restates the work in the order it was built and offers to go further

language_observations.summary: a formula is handed over with a fixed turn: therefore we can conclude, thus are as follows, it can be visualized by the equation
a result is conceded and then bounded: the gain is not evident, the reason is given, and the harm is said to stay within what the system can absorb
a fault is raised and withdrawn in one move: suitable for the simple case, however expected to run into trouble
the letter opens on its data and closes on an offer: we look forward to going further into the model

visualization_observations.summary: figure 6: the five lakes as one chain, flow running one way to the ocean
figure 9: the two controllers with their switches and the forecast module
figure 13: the best-level band against the 2017 levels
figure 15: the levels after heavy rain with the dams in place

judge_relevance_hypotheses.summary: a judge looking for a usable plan gets a monthly target, a named controller and a letter to the board that would adopt it
the memo is addressed to the body that manages the lakes, which is the reader a judge stands in for

weaknesses.summary: the flow formula grows with the head root while the prose says the river level moves against it
the freight score rewards a larger head, against the sentence above it
the rewritten channel formula carries the width twice, so its power is not the eight thirds of the next line
the lagged reach drops the square root and the gravity factor, and the prose points the lag at an equation with none
the tuning score sums over four lakes while the chain has five
the leisure score cannot vary over the twelve months it claims to summarise
meltwater and human withdrawals are named as drivers and never enter the balance
the switch to accumulated correction is cited one formula number off
the ice test with the dams repeats the account without them
the prose swaps the meanings of the two symbols in the channel formula

independent_extensions.summary: the same five weights offered retuned by season for the lowest lake, the side river and the city

why the freight score rewards a larger head

why the ice-test paragraphs repeat each other
